terms.definition: An umbrella term for computer systems that do tasks we normally associate with human thinking, such as understanding language, recognising images or making predictions.
terms.example: Spam filters, route planners and ChatGPT are all forms of AI.

terms.definition: A type of AI that learns patterns from lots of examples, instead of following rules written by a person. It makes best guesses on new cases.
terms.example: Accounting software suggesting the category for a bank transaction.

terms.definition: Machine learning using large, many-layered neural networks. Behind modern image recognition, speech transcription and LLMs.
A system of many simple maths units connected in layers, loosely inspired by the brain, whose connection strengths are adjusted during training.
A deep-learning model trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next word. It can draft, summarise, extract and answer questions in natural language.
terms.example: The models inside Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini.

terms.definition: AI that creates new content (text, images, audio, video or code) rather than only sorting or scoring existing content.
The adjustable numbers inside a model that are set during training. Large language models have billions of them.
When an AI model produces information that sounds confident and plausible but is false or made up.
terms.example: Quoting a building regulation clause that doesn't exist.

terms.definition: The model is the AI engine (e.g. a GPT or Claude model); the product is the app or service built around it (e.g. ChatGPT or Claude.ai). Products change their models over time.
Software that follows fixed, human-written rules: same input, same output every time. Not AI, but often the backbone of AI workflows.
terms.example: Copy every new web-form enquiry into a spreadsheet.

terms.definition: The examples a machine-learning model learns from. An LLM's training data is a vast collection of text; a spam filter's is a set of labelled emails.
A chat-based product, built on an LLM, that you can ask to write, summarise, analyse or answer questions.
